shared_elements: low-relief carving on a tall upright pillar/stele
row of repeated animal or creature figures in an upper register
horizontal band/register divider running across the surface
quadruped animal in profile in the middle zone
bird-like creature in the lower zone
schematic anthropomorphic/animal figures with prominent heads
repeated small vertical hatch-like signs forming a band
justification: Both surfaces are tall upright slabs bearing low-relief figural imagery organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a row of repeated creature heads/figures across the top, a band of small repeated marks beneath, profile quadrupeds in the middle zone and a large bird-like figure at the bottom — a fairly specific shared compositional scheme in a comparably schematic, flat-relief, outline-and-plain-infill manner. The differences lie in the individual motifs: A's figures include more angular, ladder-like and abstract geometric elements and denser, more crowded overlapping forms, while B's are sparser, rounder and more clearly readable as distinct animals, so the specific creatures cannot be matched one-to-one.
